speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe what happens just before you wake up frightened? Do you see anything strange or feel like someone is near your bed?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Has your child ever experienced these frightening episodes as a young child before, and do the episodes ever happen during the day when you are awake?

REQUEST TEST: Sleep_history_assessment

REQUEST IMAGES: Pediatric_sleep_study

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Sleep History Assessment indicates a 2-month history of recurrent nocturnal frightening episodes occurring 1-2 times per week. Episodes are characterized by yelling and crying upon waking without subsequent confusion; the child is consolable and appears more fatigued the following day. No prior childhood history or daytime occurrence of such episodes has been reported. Polysomnography is not indicated at this stage based on history and normal physical examination.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Met all developmental milestones with no significant medical history. Social history: Attends school regularly, with usual playing habits and interactions with peers. Lives with both parents.

speaker: Patient
text: No significant findings in other systems. No history of trauma or significant stress identified. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is highly unusual, as Pyelonephritis typically presents with fever, flank pain, and urinary symptoms rather than isolated nocturnal frights; can you confirm if she has had any fever, chills, or painful urination? Did anyone observe her eyes rolling back or muscle stiffening during these episodes?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis
